title: Pinned real Ribasim saveat-driven allocation-clock sensitivity

sequencing.scientific_dependency: DUMMY-19E run 35616065964 established that hourly saveat invalidates the one-day frozen-allocation assumption.

purpose: Quantify whether solver output frequency changes management allocation and physical hydrology when allocation.dt is held fixed at one day. This isolates output-clock coupling as a first-class model semantic rather than treating the DUMMY-19E failure as a one-off configuration accident.

independent_hybrid_reference.derivation: At every saveat-capped allocation solve, current excess Basin storage above the priority-1 1.0 m level target is available to the LP over the next represented interval. The resulting allocation is then physically realized with the common min_level reduction until the next solve.

hypotheses: With allocation.dt fixed at 86400 s, changing solver.saveat changes how often allocation is re-solved in the pinned implementation.
Shorter saveat therefore makes physically retained water available to management sooner within the same one-day horizon.
Total physical UserDemand supply increases monotonically as saveat decreases from 86400 to 3600 s.
Final Basin storage gain decreases correspondingly, while the 32 m3 external fixed-inflow ledger remains closed.
Priority changes recipient identity but not total physical supply or Basin trajectory for a given saveat because total managed availability and common physical reduction are shared.
At saveat=3600 s, both priority cases end with full 40/20 allocation after repeated within-day re-optimization.
At saveat=86400 s, the original 32/0 versus 12/20 priority allocation remains frozen for the day.
An output-frequency setting is therefore not observationally neutral in this pinned allocation configuration.
forbidden: no changing allocation.dt across sweep cases
no changing solver.saveat for any reason other than the preregistered sweep
no post-output tuning of hybrid references
no claim yet whether the observed coupling is intended behavior or a Ribasim defect
